newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen steel workers to suspend strike.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen steel workers to suspend strike.

text.p: Thousands of steel workers at Thyssen Stahl AG who downed tools this week to protest a hostile takeover attempt by rival Krupp are expected to return to work, the works council said on Wednesday.

Following an announcement that Krupp and Thyssen were to begin talks aimed at forming a joint steel company, possibly averting a takeover by Krupp, the works council said it now wanted to await the outcome of the talks.
Asked if this meant the spontaneous walk-out would end, Thyssen Stahl works council head Dieter Kroll told a gathering of Thyssen Stahl workers in Duisburg, "Yes, I think so."
He added that there would still be a gathering of workers as planned on Friday held together with the Krupp workers.
"We need the facts before us before we can decide on our position," he said. "The problems won't just be wiped off the table. We are watching this process critically."
Earlier, Krupp and Thyssen said they planned eight days of meetings to develop a common plan to create a jointly-owned steel company.
Should those talks fail, the two companies would return to the starting blocks and Krupp would probably renew its bid to Thyssen shareholders.
